name: hashcat
plain: `hashcat` is a very fast hash cracker. Like john it scrambles guesses and compares them with a hash, but it uses your graphics card, which can be hundreds of times faster.
You must tell hashcat two things: the hash type with -m (a number, such as 0 for MD5 or 1000 for NTLM) and the attack mode with -a (0 wordlist, 3 mask, 6/7 hybrid).
Cracked results are kept in a pot file; use --show to see them again.
when: Crack hashes quickly when a GPU is available.
Mask attacks when you know the password shape (for example 8 characters, last two digits).
Crack NTLM, Kerberos, WPA and many other formats.

examples.title: Wordlist attack on MD5
examples.explain: -m 0 means MD5, -a 0 means wordlist. If a hash cracks it appears and goes to the pot file.

examples.title: Find the right -m number
examples.explain: The help lists every hash mode with its number. Or use hashid / hash-identifier to guess the type first.

examples.title: Show cracked passwords
examples.explain: Reads the pot file and prints hash:password pairs without cracking again.

examples.title: Wordlist plus rules
examples.explain: -r applies a rule file that mutates every word. best64 is a small, effective set.

examples.title: Mask attack: 6 lowercase then 2 digits
examples.explain: ?l is a lowercase letter, ?d a digit, ?u uppercase, ?s symbol, ?a anything. You describe the shape and hashcat tries all.

examples.title: Hybrid: word + digits
examples.explain: Attack mode 6 takes each word and appends three digits (sunshine123).

examples.title: Benchmark your machine
examples.explain: Shows hashes per second for a hash type.

examples.title: Run on CPU only
examples.explain: -D 1 selects CPU devices. Useful in a VM without a GPU. You may need --force on some VMs (use with care).

examples.title: Resume a session
examples.cmd:
hashcat --session ctf1 -m 0 -a 0 hashes.txt rockyou.txt
hashcat --session ctf1 --restore
examples.explain: A named session can be stopped and continued later.

options.plain: Hash type number (0 MD5, 100 SHA1, 1000 NTLM, 1400 SHA256, 1800 sha512crypt, 3200 bcrypt, 13100 Kerberoast...).
0 straight (wordlist), 1 combination, 3 brute force/mask, 6 wordlist+mask, 7 mask+wordlist, 9 association.

mistakes: Choosing the wrong -m number: the run ends with 'token length exception' or just never cracks. Use --example-hashes or hashid to be sure.
Forgetting that mask attacks cost time exponentially: ?a x 9 is huge.
Running without a GPU driver and wondering why it is slow; check hashcat -I.
Using --force as a habit: it hides real problems.
Expecting results to print twice: cracked hashes are in the pot, use --show.
try: Hash 'sunshine1' with echo -n sunshine1 | md5sum and crack it with a mask and with rockyou.
Compare rockyou with and without best64.rule on a small list.
Use --keyspace to compare the size of ?l?l?l?l?l?l and ?a?a?a?a?a?a.
see_also: john(8), hashid(1), hash-identifier(1), hashcat-utils, and the wordlists in /usr/share/wordlists.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
